newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BONDS END STEADY, OUTLOOK NERVOUS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BONDS END STEADY, OUTLOOK NERVOUS.

text.p: 1655/1355 GMT - Bonds end thin Friday trade little changed as
many operators hesitate to take up fresh positions with most of
Europe closed for holidays on Monday. Jitters too ahead of Fed's
FOMC meeting, and dealers say Sweden seen likely to say at
end-May it will stay outside first group of EMU countries.
*FIM-06 yld pct 6.10 vs 6.09 *06 gap over Bund bps 38 vs 37
*FIM-04 yld pct 5.67 vs 5.65 *FIM-99 yld pct 3.72 vs 3.70
*Jun FRAs 3.11 pct vs 3.12 *March FRAs 3.76 pct vs 3.79
*SEK/FIM 0.6750 vs 0.6680 *ECU index 101.08 vs 100.73
Bonds closed a lacklustre Friday
session little changed with many investors reluctant to take up
new positions ahead of a long weekend in most of Europe a day
before the U.S. Fed meets on monetary policy, dealers said.
"Trade will be very thin in the early part of the week as
Europe is closed for holidays on Monday, and on Tuesday there
will be the much-awaited FOMC meeting," one dealer said.
The market was split on whether the Federal Reserve would
raise interest rates at the meeting, so operators expected any
gains to be capped ahead of it.
Dealers also expressed concern that Sweden was likely to
remain outside the first group of EMU countries, which they said
would have a negative impact on markets here.
"Some overseas investors could interpret that as dampening
Finland's chances of an early entry to EMU," one said.
"The (Finnish parliamentary) opposition has listed Sweden's
entry as a pre-requisite (for Finland to join) -- there is
likely to be some upheaval here when Sweden says it won't be
among the first," he added.
The Swedish government has said it will announce its view on
membership of European economic and monetary union sometime
between May 23-31.
